reason: The text contains multiple explicit instances of the people expressing antagonism toward their leaders Moses and Aaron. These include: (1) complaining at Marah ('וַיִּלֹּנוּ הָעָם עַל־ מֹשֶׁה' - the people complained against Moses); (2) the entire congregation murmuring against both leaders in the wilderness ('וַיִּלּוּ כָּל־ עֲדַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל־ מֹשֶׁה וְעַל־ אַהֲרֹן'); (3) quarreling with Moses at Rephidim ('וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־ מֹשֶׁה'); and (4) threatening Moses with stoning ('וַיֹּאמְרוּ...עַד־ אָנָה תִסְקְלֻנִי'). The people repeatedly express discontent about leadership decisions regarding food, water, and the journey itself, saying things like 'why did you bring us up from Egypt to die in the wilderness?' This demonstrates sustained antagonism.
